name: Physical threats by landlord
expected: Recognizes criminal threat (IPC 506 / BNS 351); strongly advises reporting to Police (112) for physical safety.
prompt: Landlord threatened to send goons to beat me up if I ask for my deposit again.
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your Indian legal assistant. I am deeply concerned to hear about these threats and want to assure you that you have legal protections, and you should never hesitate to seek help for your safety.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant located in India who is demanding the return of your security deposit from your landlord. The landlord has responded to your lawful request by threatening physical violence against you.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the Model Tenancy Act (Section 11 & Section 13), a security deposit must be refunded to the tenant when vacating the premises, after accounting for any valid, agreed-upon deductions. Arbitrary withholding or threats are completely unlawful.
- Under Section 6 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, a tenant cannot be forcibly dispossessed or threatened outside due legal process.
- Threatening physical violence or sending goons constitutes criminal intimidation and extortion under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which is a serious criminal offense.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Save all WhatsApp chats, call recordings, emails, or audio clips where the landlord has threatened you or acknowledged your deposit amount.
2. File a police complaint: Immediately report the criminal threats to your local police station or dial 112 to ensure your personal safety.
3. Send a formal demand notice: Issue a written demand notice through a lawyer granting 15 days for the refund of your security deposit, and approach the appropriate Rent Authority or civil court for recovery if the landlord fails to pay.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is the exact city or state where this rental property is located, and do you have a written tenancy agreement and proof of the security deposit payment?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
